title: Global data centre construction to peak in 2030
gist: Oxford Economics forecasts data centre construction across its 25 markets will grow 45% to peak at US$212bn in 2030, then fall 40% by 2037 (still over 3x 2022 levels). The US drives over 60% of near-term growth via hyperscalers, but construction labour shortages cap pipeline delivery and Democratic wins could tighten state and local permitting.

themes.theme: Data centre construction cycle: 2030 peak, then 40% decline

insights.claim: Oxford Economics forecasts data centre construction work done across its 25 forecast markets will grow 45% over the next four years to peak at US$212bn in 2030.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Sets a dated peak for the data centre capex build-out; construction, materials and electrical equipment suppliers face a cyclical top around 2030.
insights.quote: grow 45% over the next four years to peak at US$212bn in 2030

insights.claim: After peaking in 2030, global data centre construction activity is forecast to fall 40% through 2037 while still remaining more than three times its 2022 level.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Signals a post-2030 downturn for data-centre-exposed builders and suppliers; valuations extrapolating the boom past 2030 look vulnerable, though the base stays structurally elevated.
insights.quote: Construction activity will then fall 40% through to 2037 but remain more than three times the 2022 level.

themes.theme: US hyperscaler dominance and geographic leaders

insights.claim: The US is the largest data centre construction market and will account for over 60% of global data centre construction spending growth over the next two years, with China the second-largest market.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Near-term data centre construction upside is concentrated in the US; exposure to US contractors and grid equipment captures most of the growth.
insights.quote: will account for over 60% of global spending growth over the next two years
insights.locator: The US remains the largest market

insights.claim: Data centre construction activity continues to be driven by tech giants Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Google and OpenAI building data centres for their own use.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Construction demand hinges on hyperscaler and AI-lab capex guidance; any capex pullback by these five directly hits the construction pipeline.
insights.locator: The US remains the largest market

insights.claim: Australia will be the fastest-growing data centre construction market through 2028, with Ireland the second fastest-growing.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Australia and Ireland are the highest-growth non-US geographies for data centre builders, developers and power infrastructure plays.

themes.theme: Construction labour bottleneck caps the pipeline

insights.claim: New data centre announcements far exceed the construction industry's capacity to deliver, as tight construction labour markets limit how many projects can break ground and cause cost escalation and delays on live projects.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Announced data centre pipelines overstate realisable capacity; expect delivery slippage, higher project costs and pricing power for contractors and skilled trades.
insights.quote: New data centre announcements far exceed the capability of the construction industry to deliver the pipeline.

themes.theme: US political and local permitting risk

insights.claim: Sweeping Democratic electoral victories in the US risk greater restrictions on the next wave of data centre projects, with the risk concentrated at state and local level where governors, utility regulators and zoning boards control rates, incentives, permitting and grid access.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Watch state-level utility rate cases, tax incentive rollbacks and zoning fights as leading indicators of US data centre project attrition.
insights.quote: We think this risk is more prevalent at the state and local level where governors, utility regulators, and zoning boards set the rates, incentives, permitting and grid access
